title: Effects of high-pressure synthesis on phase formation and superconducting properties of PrFeAsO1-xFx
authors: Priya Singh, Konrad Kwatek, Tatiana Zajarniuk, Tomasz Cetner, Jan Mizeracki, Shiv J. Singh
abstract: Motivated by recent reports of enhanced superconducting performance in several families of iron-based superconductors (IBS) processed by high-pressure (HP) synthesis, we investigate the influence of high gas pressure and high-temperature synthesis (HP-HTS) process on the structural, microstructural, electrical transport, and magnetic properties of Pr-based oxypnictide PrFeAsO1-xFx (Pr1111) using the processing conditions of 0.5 GPa for 1 h previously optimized for other IBS families. Representative underdoped (x = 0.2), optimal doped (x = 0.3), and overdoped (x = 0.5) compositions from the ambient-pressure electronic phase diagram of Pr1111 are selected to evaluate its composition-dependent effects of HP-HTS. The results demonstrate that HP-HTS enhances fluorine incorporation, improves phase formation, and produces a denser microstructure with improved grain connectivity in the underdoped and optimal doped compositions. Magnetic measurements reveal increased in the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) of ~1 K for x = 0.2 and ~6 K for x = 0.3, whereas only a marginal improvement in the critical current density is observed. Electrical resistivity measurements of the underdoped composition show a slight increase in Tc accompanied by a broader resistive transition, indicating residual structural inhomogeneity. In contrast, the overdoped composition exhibits increased impurity phase segregation, accompanied by suppression of superconductivity. These results demonstrate that the effectiveness of HP-HTS in Pr1111 is strongly composition dependent and governed by the interplay among fluorine incorporation, phase stability, and microstructural evolution, highlighting the need for further optimization of the HP-HTS processing conditions.
summary: This experimental work investigates how high-pressure synthesis modifies the superconducting performance of $	ext{PrFeAsO}_{1-x}	ext{F}_x$. The findings show that while high pressure improves crystal structure and raises $	ext{T}_c$ at optimal doping, this enhancement is highly sensitive to fluorine content; excessive doping leads to detrimental impurity phase formation.
main_problem: The study investigates how high-pressure/high-temperature synthesis (HP-HTS) affects the structural, superconducting, and magnetic properties of fluorine-doped iron pnictide superconductors ($	ext{PrFeAsO}_{1-x}	ext{F}_x$).
main_result: HP-HTS enhances superconductivity ($	ext{T}_c$ increase) and microstructure in underdoped/optimal compositions by improving fluorine incorporation, but this benefit is lost in overdoped samples due to impurity phase segregation.
method: The research combines synthesis (ambient vs. high pressure), structural characterization (XRD, lattice parameter refinement), microstructural analysis (SEM), and transport measurements ($ho(T)$, $M(H)$) across different doping levels.
model_or_system: The physical system is the iron-based superconductor $	ext{PrFeAsO}_{1-x}	ext{F}_x$, which exhibits superconductivity dependent on fluorine substitution ($x$) and processing conditions. The study maps out the superconducting dome by testing underdoped, optimal, and overdoped regimes.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($	ext{T}_c$), critical current density ($	ext{J}_c$), lattice parameters ($a$, $c$), fluorine incorporation level ($x_{	ext{act}}$), and phase purity (secondary phases like $	ext{PrOF}$).
important_parameters: Doping concentration ($x=0.2, 0.3, 0.5$), synthesis pressure (0.5 GPa), temperature (950°C), and the interplay between fluorine content and phase stability.
main_assumptions: The effectiveness of HP-HTS is assumed to be governed by achieving optimal fluorine incorporation without exceeding the solubility limit, which dictates structural integrity and superconducting performance.
figures_summary: Figures detail XRD patterns comparing synthesis methods, track lattice parameter changes with doping, show SEM images contrasting microstructures (porosity/connectivity), and plot $	ext{T}_c$ derived from both resistivity and magnetization measurements versus fluorine concentration.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares samples synthesized under ambient pressure versus high pressure. It analyzes structural improvements (phase purity, densification) first, followed by quantitative measurements of superconducting properties ($	ext{T}_c$, $	ext{J}_c$) across the doping spectrum to establish composition-dependent limits.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter superconductivity, the systematic study of phase stability and structural modification under extreme conditions (high pressure) provides insights into how external thermodynamic variables can tune electronic properties in correlated materials.
